castleSections.title: Your family is a castle on a hill
castleSections.body: Inside the castle are the people, values, resources, and peace you care about most. When addiction is active and there are no boundaries, the castle has no defenses: anyone can walk in, take what they want, and leave wreckage behind. Bills disappear, trust erodes, and the whole household orbits the crisis. Boundaries don't remove love. They protect what matters.

castleSections.title: The walls — what is non-negotiable
castleSections.body: Walls are the firm limits that keep danger out: "No drugs or alcohol in this house." "We will not lie for you or cover up DUIs." "You cannot stay here if you are violent or refusing all help." These are not threats. They state what is allowed inside the family. A clear wall you follow through on also ends the exhausting re-negotiation.

castleSections.title: The moat — emotional & physical distance
castleSections.body: The moat is the space that keeps you from being pulled into every emergency, lie, or manipulation: not answering middle-of-the-night calls unless it's a real safety issue, not arguing in circles with someone intoxicated. This distance can feel like not caring. It isn't. It lets you respond instead of react, and it doesn't cut your loved one off from help.

castleSections.title: The drawbridge — when and how you engage
castleSections.body: The drawbridge is your choice. Lower it for honest conversations, treatment planning, sober visits, therapy. Raise it when your loved one is intoxicated, abusive, demanding money, or refusing all responsibility. Enabling is leaving it down all the time. Healthy support says: "We will meet you on the bridge when you are reaching for recovery. We will not let your addiction storm the castle."

castleSections.title: Maintenance — keeping the castle strong
castleSections.body: Castles need upkeep. It's easy to slip: lending money "just this once," letting substances back in, softening agreed consequences. Regular family check-ins (often with a professional) catch cracks early. The goal isn't to punish. It's to make use less comfortable while the door to change stays open.

castleSections.title: Guardians, not hostages
castleSections.body: You can't control whether your loved one chooses recovery. You can control your walls, your moat, and your drawbridge. The message stays clear: "We love you deeply. We will not participate in your destruction. We will stand ready to welcome you when you choose a different path." Boundaries aren't harsh or selfish. They are love that survives addiction.

castleSections.title: Anchored in answers, not emotions
castleSections.body: Anger fades, guilt creeps in, fear spikes at 2 AM. A boundary built on emotion shifts with it. Build yours on honest answers to two questions: Have I enabled the addiction in any way? Has the addiction harmed me in any way? If either answer is yes, the boundary isn't optional, and it isn't cruel. Answer both below.

anchor1.question: Have I enabled the addiction in any way?
anchor1.sub: This is bedrock, not blame. Tap all that apply.

e-fin.reason: Money given "to help" funds the disease.
e-fin.wall: I will no longer give cash, pay bills, or cover debts created by the addiction.

e-emo.wall: I will no longer make excuses for them or rescue them from the consequences of their use.

e-sil.reason: Silence is a vote for more of the same.
e-sil.wall: I will no longer keep secrets about the addiction or pretend I don't see what I see.

anchor2.question: Has the addiction harmed me in any way?
anchor2.sub: Your harm is real and it counts. Tap all that apply.

h-fin.reason: Drained savings, stolen items, mounting debt.
h-fin.wall: I will protect my money: separate accounts, no shared cards, no loans.

h-emo.reason: Manipulation, broken promises, walking on eggshells.
h-emo.wall: I will end any conversation that becomes manipulative or cruel, and revisit it when we're both calm.

h-phys.wall: If I feel unsafe, I will leave immediately and call for help. My safety comes first.

builder.sub: Tap a suggestion above or write your own. State what you will do.

walls.empty: No boundaries yet. Use a suggestion or write one clear limit.
walls.shareDirect: Share walls with the on-call coach
walls.deleteBody: This deletes the boundary and its follow-through notes from your account. It can't be undone.

challenge.monday: It's Monday. Join Family Squares on Zoom tonight at 7:00 PM Pacific, with people who understand.
daily: Say "no" once today, and don't explain yourself afterward.
Write down one limit you held this week. Notice how it felt.
Take a 20-minute walk without your phone. Just you and your thoughts.
Tell someone who supports you "I appreciate you." A text counts.
Name one responsibility you carry that belongs to someone else.
Make a good meal just for you today. Sit down and taste it.
Write a single sentence you can say the next time someone pressures you.
Do something for 30 minutes that has nothing to do with your loved one.
Check in with your body. Running on empty? Do one thing to refuel.
Name one enabling behavior you want to change. Write it down, just for you.
Reach out to one person who supports you, even just to say hello.
When you want to rescue someone today, pause and ask: "Is this mine to carry?"
Let yourself rest today. No problem-solving, just rest.
Write down your three most important values. Do your actions show them today?
Plan one small thing to look forward to this week. Put it in your calendar.
Tell yourself out loud: "I am doing the best I can. That is enough."
Recall one time you said yes but wanted to say no. What stopped you?
Set a technology-free hour this evening. Read, draw, or just sit.
Write two sentences about why you are doing this hard work.
Do a physical reset: stretch, take a bath, or breathe deeply for five minutes.
Recall one moment this week when a limit you held kept the peace.
Notice one thing today that you're grateful for that has nothing to do with recovery.
Write one sentence you would say to a close friend in your exact situation.
Think of someone who gives you energy. Spend time with them today.
Celebrate one small win from this week, however minor.
Spend 10 minutes in complete silence. No phone. No background noise. Just you.
Write down three things you love about yourself that have nothing to do with caregiving.
Let yourself feel what you're feeling today without trying to fix or change it.
Do one thing today just for your own joy, and don't apologize for it.

enabling.heading: Am I enabling?

results.r0: This week you held strong limits. Stay consistent.
results.low: A few moments worth noticing. Patterns start small.
results.mid: Common, but worth addressing. Review your walls this week.
results.high: Worth taking seriously. Consider talking with your coach.

sets: Did you give money that might have been used on substances?
Did you make excuses or cover for them to others?
Did you let a limit be crossed without a consequence?
Did you avoid bringing up their use to keep the peace?
Did you take on a responsibility that belongs to them?
Did you minimize or rationalize their behavior to yourself or others?
Did you decide out of fear of their reaction, not what felt right?
Did you rescue them from a consequence of their own making?
Did you give them another chance after a broken promise without any real change?
Did you stay in a situation that felt unsafe rather than leave?
Did you put their needs entirely ahead of your own all week?
Did you plan next steps on their behalf without being asked?
Did you accept an excuse for behavior you normally would not tolerate?
Did you feel responsible for their emotional state this week?
Did you cancel your own plans because of their behavior?
Did you skip getting support so you wouldn't feel disloyal?
Did you try to control their use: hiding it, pouring it out, or counting it?
Did you feel as though their choices were somehow your fault?

intro: Castle walls are agreed boundaries: clear limits on what you will and won't do to stay safe and well. Write yours first, then invite family to agree. You don't need your loved one's permission.
